title: Durable ProofPath ingestion crosses the LiminalDB persistence frontier without authority escalation

ideaContract.purpose: Independently verify that canonical ProofPath evidence accepted at the SYSTEM-004 boundary can cross into durable local/test LiminalDB storage, survive restart, deduplicate ambiguous retries, preserve bi-temporal identity and remain non-authorizing for execution or external effects.
ideaContract.expectedOutcome: The same native SYSTEM-004 logical operation is accepted by the canonical artifact validator, granted a separate local/test storage admission, written through the canonical ProofPathDurableLedger, reproduced byte-for-byte after process restart, retried without a second durable effect, rejected when evidence changes under the same operation, and accepted by native LTP strict trace replay.
invariants: the SYSTEM-004 logical_operation_id is inherited unchanged through durable ingestion
artifact validation remains distinct from storage admission
the exact ProofPath capability identity remains bound to the persisted evidence
LiminalDB artifact-contract provenance remains distinct from current AuditEvent semantic compatibility identity
valid_time and first durable transaction_time remain separately replayable
the exact accepted AuditEvent and admission-report bytes survive process restart
same operation plus same semantic artifact produces no second durable record
same operation plus changed semantic artifact fails closed
post-sync acknowledgement ambiguity cannot produce a duplicate durable effect after reopen and retry
local/test persistence grants no execution, mutation or external-effect authority
the agent trajectory through persistence is independently inspectable and replayable
forbiddenOutcomes: treating the SYSTEM-004 dry-run artifact PASS as ambient persistence authority
renaming the upstream logical operation for the durable stage
deriving the durable idempotency key from payload bytes so changed evidence silently becomes a new operation
creating a second durable record after a synced-but-unacknowledged append
rewriting the first transaction_time on an idempotent retry
accepting changed evidence under the same operation key
allowing persistence metadata to grant execution or external-effect authority
claiming durable verification from a final object whose LTP trajectory is invalid

evidence.claim: SYSTEM-004 supplies the native ProofPath VALID receipt and dedicated LiminalDB AuditEvent while explicitly stopping before persistence.
The canonical LiminalDB durable consumer stores exact accepted event and admission bytes in a local/test WAL namespace with replay-enforced provenance, temporal, idempotency and authority invariants.

evidence.ref: FCRP-SYSTEM-005 workflow / separate-process inspect and byte comparison
evidence.claim: A new process reopens the WAL and reproduces the exact original AuditEvent and admission report bytes with the original valid_time and first transaction_time.

evidence.ref: FCRP-SYSTEM-005 workflow / retry, conflict and AfterSyncBeforeAck tests
evidence.claim: Same semantic retry returns ALREADY_PRESENT, changed evidence under the same operation returns IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, and post-sync acknowledgement ambiguity recovers to one durable record after reopen.
The durable-ingestion trajectory is accepted by the pinned native LTP strict inspector and deterministic replay.

past.summary: SYSTEM-004 proved native ProofPath to LiminalDB artifact compatibility and explicitly stopped at the persistence frontier because no dedicated durable ProofPath consumer was canonical.

present.summary: LiminalDB now exposes a canonical local/test ProofPathDurableLedger. SYSTEM-005 independently consumes that exact capability and tests durable append, restart replay, idempotent recovery, conflict rejection, temporal preservation and path admissibility. valid_time and transaction_time are verified as evidence fields inside the causal sequence; FCRP v0.2 does not elevate them to protocol time domains.

future.summary: Production ingestion, distributed replication, rollback resistance against mutually consistent history replacement, retention/compaction and tenant authorization remain separate gates and cannot be inferred from local/test durability.

causalPath.statement: Artifact acceptance cannot itself grant persistence; a distinct local/test storage admission must authorize only the storage write while execution and external-effect authority remain false.
SYSTEM-004 therefore correctly stops at a persistence frontier: artifact acceptance is verified, but no durable state transition has yet been independently exercised by the system verifier.
The canonical ProofPathDurableLedger is used as the narrow durable boundary, keyed by namespace plus inherited logical operation and backed by the existing LiminalDB WAL durability primitive.
After a real local WAL append and process restart, exact accepted event/admission bytes, valid_time and first transaction_time are replayed from durable state.
A same-semantic retry is deduplicated, changed evidence under the same operation is rejected, and a synced-but-unacknowledged append recovers to one durable effect after reopen.
The independent durable-ingestion path is accepted by native LTP strict inspection and replay without widening authority beyond local/test storage.

navigation.reason: The missing guarantee is a cross-repository consumer transition from verified evidence into durable local/test storage, plus the recovery and trajectory contracts around that transition.

refactor.change: Consume the canonical LiminalDB ProofPathDurableLedger only after separate local/test storage admission, preserving the SYSTEM-004 operation identity and zero execution/external-effect authority.
refactor.expectedEffect: The persistence frontier becomes a real, independently replayed local/test durable transition rather than a diagrammatic claim, while production persistence and execution authority remain unproven and unauthorized.

authorization.authorityBoundary: SYSTEM-005 may exercise only an ephemeral local/test LiminalDB storage write under an explicit test-harness admission. It grants no production database write, repository mutation, deployment, financial action, external effect or execution authority.
